# ADR 0029: Keep destructive CAD freshness host-owned

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-08-30
- Owners: Make skill, runtime, and workflow maintainers
- Relates to: ADR 0027 (all-printable preflight), ADR 0028 (deep economics)

## Context

The first deep-economics Quest run, Comet Choir, preserved a full mechanism
coupon and CAD project across a 30-minute Make timeout. Its recovery correctly
reused those bytes, but the iterative `verify_project --print-preflight
--fresh` command failed inside the product-run sandbox. Generated files could
be removed while macOS denied `rmdir` on an empty `__cadgen__` component
directory. The verifier raised `PermissionError`, the native turn failed, and
no proposal or publication occurred.

The same run also showed that proving mechanics alone is insufficient. Its
exact render was mechanically structured but visually read as a faceted blob
attached to a flat board, with floating play pieces. Spending on full exports
before falsifying the held form worked against both quality and economics.

## Decision

Native Make iteration runs `verify_project <project> --print-preflight` without
`--fresh`. Source-closure freshness regenerates changed targets in the product
sandbox. The trusted isolated host remains the only authority that performs a
destructive `--fresh --exports --strict-fit` rebuild before accepting Made.

The shared verifier still supports `--fresh`. Its cache remover deletes every
generated byte and symlink, while tolerating sandbox-protected directories only
when their entire remaining tree is byte-free. Any undeletable generated byte
continues to fail closed.

Forge and Quest also add an early form falsifier: before detailed parts, Make
renders the cheapest exact volumetric blockout from the required held and
signature views. The blockout must communicate identity and the defining
relationship without names or copy. Blob-plus-board, plaque, floating-piece,
or explanation-dependent reads are repaired or simplified at that boundary.

## Consequences

- Native iteration no longer spends a recovery turn on a forbidden directory
  deletion that the host will repeat authoritatively anyway.
- Frozen exact source and generated artifacts remain subject to the same final
  host rebuild and byte comparison; no gate or freshness claim is weakened.
- Empty protected cache directories are not treated as product evidence.
- Deep efforts spend on detailed CAD only after both the causal relationship
  and the visible product form survive cheap falsification.
- No Python aesthetic judge, stage, model call, or retry loop is introduced.

## Verification

- Cache-cleanup tests cover the protected-empty-directory fallback and refuse
  undeletable generated bytes.
- Product-run asset tests require host-owned fresh-rebuild guidance, correct
  `gen`/`export` syntax, and the early volumetric blockout.
- The complete strict repository suite must pass before this decision ships.
